To prevent DNS rebinding attacks, you can implement the following techniques:

1. Validate Subdomains: Ensure that the subdomain input is properly validated before using it to generate a URL. In the provided code example, the `isValidSubdomain` function checks the length and characters of the subdomain to prevent malicious input.

2. Same-Origin Policy: Enforce the Same-Origin Policy in your web application to restrict scripts from one origin accessing resources from a different origin. This helps prevent malicious scripts from accessing sensitive information.

3. Use Content Security Policy (CSP): Implement CSP headers in your web application to control which resources can be loaded by the browser. This can help prevent unauthorized scripts from executing on your domain.

4. Set DNS Rebinding Protection: Configure your DNS server to prevent DNS rebinding attacks by setting appropriate DNS configurations, such as setting a short TTL (Time to Live) for DNS records and using DNS pinning techniques.

5. Network Segmentation: Implement network segmentation to isolate different parts of your network and prevent unauthorized access between them. This can help mitigate the impact of DNS rebinding attacks.

By incorporating these techniques into your application and network infrastructure, you can reduce the risk of DNS rebinding attacks and enhance the security of your system.
